references.text: Achan confesses his sin and tells what he took from the devoted things.
Achan and his family are punished for taking from the devoted things, and the Lord's anger subsides.
Joshua gives orders that everything in Jericho is to be devoted to the Lord, and warns against taking anything from it.
Reference to Achan who committed treachery regarding the devoted things, and how this affected all Israel.
Prohibition against bringing any detestable thing into the house, as it would also become devoted.
Similar expressions that the Lord's anger was kindled against Israel because of disobedience.
The Lord's anger was kindled against Israel because of sin, and punishment followed.
Zerah's son is mentioned in Judah's genealogy, who is Achan's ancestor.
